summary: Build, all 40 tests, and both linters pass. No implementation defect was confirmed against the approved recovery criteria. Verification of the no-deployment requirement remains blocked by the absence of a complete run-wide action record; repository inspection alone cannot establish that negative action.

findings.title: No run-wide evidence to verify the no-deployment requirement
findings.description: REQ-017 and TC-026 require a review of delivery actions for any performed application deployment. The coding report explicitly calls the run-wide action history unavailable, and the review assessment likewise does not provide one. The diff from 50b661e57973de16a23e801e305160a08b0ae01d contains no deployment workflow or deployment-performing configuration, but this only establishes the repository-side REQ-018 check, not whether a deployment occurred outside the repository. This is an unverified acceptance criterion, not evidence that anyone deployed the app.
findings.recommendation: Obtain and review the complete run-wide executed-action/deployment history for TC-026; only then mark REQ-017 covered if it shows no performed deployment. Preserve the verification gap if authoritative records cannot be obtained.

requirement_coverage.evidence: GET /sign-in renders the bordered sign-in panel, labels, placeholders, link, button and footer in src/password_reset_exercise/templates/sign_in.html:4-20; static/style.css:11-27,30-34,62-82,90-94 supplies observed treatments. tests/test_entry_pages.py:49-94 passes structural checks; rendered-browser image fidelity and assistive-technology checks in TC-001/002 remain manual, with no exact pixel/color requirement.
sign_in.html:17 links to Flask GET /password/forgot in __init__.py:124-127, rendering a labeled reset-request form; tests/test_entry_pages.py:125-135 verifies navigation.

__init__.py:139-151 renders the same generic confirmation for valid existing, unknown and capped requests; tests/test_request_reset.py:48-59,77-97 compares status, HTML and navigation at and below the cap and inspects nondisclosure.

state.py:110-133 counts accepted requests within (now-1 hour, now] under the shared lock; tests/test_request_reset.py:77-127 and 201-210 verify five allowed, sixth blocked, independent accounts, exact rollover and concurrent limiting.
state.py:123-133 issues an owner-bound opaque link into the private in-memory sink; tests/test_request_reset.py:130-167 verifies the recipient, link, token digest, issue time and usable reset form.
state.py:135-152 rejects consumed links and complete_reset at state.py:159-185 consumes a link under one lock; tests/test_complete_reset.py:69-122 covers replay and competing POSTs.

state.py:114-133 records the issuance timestamp; state.py:149 requires submission strictly before issued_at+30 minutes; tests/test_complete_reset.py:125-165 and tests/test_verification.py:136-195 cover immediately before, exactly at and after expiry.

__init__.py:153-182 accepts the eligible reset form; state.py:164-185 hashes and replaces only the token-bound account password; tests/test_complete_reset.py:168-251 checks new/old hashes, other-account isolation, invalid tokens and empty-input rejection.

state.py:169-176 advances the owner's generation and state.py:187-205 checks registered sessions against that generation; tests/test_complete_reset.py:168-193 and tests/test_verification.py:136-180 verify multiple old sessions rejected and another owner's session retained. No sign-in success semantics are specified or claimed.
state.py:174-185 appends an owner-directed reset_success notification before returning success; tests/test_complete_reset.py:254-286 verifies two distinct successes and no notice for rejected resets.
state.py:67-96 registers isolated synthetic accounts without identity service; tests/test_recovery_state.py:17-33,85-101 checks hashed accounts and instance isolation.

state.py:75,129-133,174-185,233-237 stores link and success notices privately in memory; tests/test_recovery_state.py:63-82 and tests/test_request_reset.py:130-167 inspect private entries and no public sink endpoints.
.python-version and pyproject.toml:5-8 declare Python 3.12 and Flask; tests/test_entry_pages.py:153-158 asserts the 3.12 runtime and working Flask factory; the full pytest gate ran on Python 3.12.3.

__init__.py:120-182 uses Flask render_template for sign-in, request, confirmation and reset states; tests/test_entry_pages.py:161-179, tests/test_request_reset.py:63-75 and tests/test_complete_reset.py:289-331 inspect populated raw HTML without JavaScript.

40 pytest tests passed, including entry/recovery parity, rolling cap and concurrency, issue-time expiry, replay, account isolation, session invalidation and per-success notification in tests/test_entry_pages.py, test_request_reset.py, test_complete_reset.py and test_verification.py. Coding tests.json lists 24/30 automated cases; TC-001/002/028/029 additionally require manual visual/keyboard/AT inspection, and TC-026/027 are delivery checks rather than pytest behavior.

README.md:59-82 states synthetic accounts, in-memory notices, process-local restart loss, cross-worker limits, missing real identity/mail/durable delivery and no production readiness; tests/test_documentation.py:6-30 checks the disclosures.

No deployment action was observed in this review and README.md:81-82 says not to deploy, but coding-report.md:42 and the assessment.md:17 record that a complete run-wide action/deployment history is unavailable. TC-026 explicitly treats absent records as unverified. See REV-001; repository diff cannot prove a negative external action.

Reviewed git diff --name-status 50b661e57973de16a23e801e305160a08b0ae01d and changed source, config and documentation: no .github/workflows path, deployment job or deployment-performing configuration was added. TC-027 is a repository inspection, not evidence about delivery actions.
